validated_results.journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology
validated_results.reason: Prediagnostic nested case-control study of stored serum vitamin D metabolites (25-D and 1,25-D) and subsequent prostate cancer diagnosis, providing a human incidence comparison.

extraction.comparison_type: Cases versus individually matched controls; risk across higher versus lower serum 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D levels
extraction.timing: prediagnostic serum collected 1964-1971 with cancer diagnosis before December 31, 1987
extraction.population: Members of the Kaiser Permanente Medical Care Plan who provided stored serum samples

cases.excerpt: Levels of 25-D and 1,25-D were measured in samples from 90 black and 91 white men diagnosed with prostate cancer before December 31, 1987 and controls individually matched on age, race, and day of serum storage.
cases.location: abstract; cases derived from reported group counts 90 + 91 = 181

p_value.excerpt: Mean serum 1,25-D was 1.81 pg/ml lower in cases than in matched controls (P = 0.002).

comparison.excerpt: Risk of prostate cancer decreased with higher levels of 1,25-D especially in men with low levels of 25-D.

design.excerpt: controls individually matched on age, race, and day of serum storage

timing.excerpt: Between 1964 and 1971, more than 250,000 serum samples were collected

continent.excerpt: Kaiser Permanente Medical Care Plan in Oakland and San Francisco

validated_results.title: Smoking, alcohol, coffee, tea, caffeine, and theobromine: risk of prostate cancer in Utah (United States).
validated_results.reason: Population-based case-control study reporting odds ratios for dietary theobromine intake and newly diagnosed prostate cancer.

extraction.comparison_type: Older men consuming 11 to 20 mg theobromine per day versus men with very low theobromine intake, all tumors
extraction.timing: cases newly diagnosed between 1983 and 1986 with exposure assessed at study interview
extraction.population: Men with newly diagnosed prostate cancer and age-matched controls, predominantly members of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints

sample_size.excerpt: Data from a population-based study of newly diagnosed cases of prostate cancer (n = 362) and age-matched controls (n = 685) conducted in Utah (United States) between 1983 and 1986 were used to determine if cigarette smoking, alcohol, coffee, tea, caffeine, and theobromine were associated with prostate cancer risk.
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 362 + 685 = 1047

cases.excerpt: Data from a population-based study of newly diagnosed cases of prostate cancer (n = 362) and age-matched controls (n = 685) conducted in Utah (United States) between 1983 and 1986 were used to determine if cigarette smoking, alcohol, coffee, tea, caffeine, and theobromine were associated with prostate cancer risk.

effect_size.excerpt: Compared with men with very low levels of theobromine intake, older men consuming 11 to 20 and over 20 mg of theobromine per day were at increased risk of prostate cancer (odds ratio [OR] for all tumors = 2.06, 95 percent confidence interval [CI] = 1.33-3.20, and OR = 1.47, CI = 0.99-2.19, respectively; OR for aggressive tumors = 1.90, CI = 0.90-3.97, and OR = 1.74, CI = 0.91-3.32, respectively).

confidence_interval.excerpt: Compared with men with very low levels of theobromine intake, older men consuming 11 to 20 and over 20 mg of theobromine per day were at increased risk of prostate cancer (odds ratio [OR] for all tumors = 2.06, 95 percent confidence interval [CI] = 1.33-3.20, and OR = 1.47, CI = 0.99-2.19, respectively; OR for aggressive tumors = 1.90, CI = 0.90-3.97, and OR = 1.74, CI = 0.91-3.32, respectively).
